description: The default brand of Brand expressive: its theme picks in each mode. The loader joins it with scheme.json.

default.label: Brand expressive
default.description: The single brand: vivid magenta, Bricolage Grotesque display, pill controls.

theme.$description: The Brand expressive theme: what each brand-dependent semantic key picks, in light and dark, plus mode-free picks (fonts, corners) in base. Info uses blue, kept apart from the brand color so it never reads as an action. Categories 1 to 5 are pink, blue, green, amber, taupe: distinct hues for tags and chart series, with no meaning. Disabled uses the neutral taupe.

open-ds.why: radius.pill: We use a pill corner for buttons and inputs in order to mark their role as controls in a playful tone, by brand convention. A full radius does this by rounding both ends into a capsule, the brand's signature shape. So every action feels bold and friendly, because the brand is bold (brand.q1), controls are pills (shape.values) and each section holds one big idea (content.q2).

radius.pill: We use the pill control corner for badges in order to keep one role family by the badge relation: badges share the control's corner. The same full radius does this by giving a status the capsule of the buttons beside it. So a status pill matches the buttons and the page keeps one shape, because badges get no corner of their own (shape.roles) and controls are pills (shape.values).

radius.20: We use a 20px corner for menu options in order to keep nesting by the relation: the 24px surface corner minus the panel's 4px padding. The inner radius does this by following the outer curve at the padding's distance. So an option's curve runs parallel to its menu's curve, because surfaces take 24px (shape.roles, brand.q1) and the panel's padding is 4px (spacing.values).

radius.12: We use the 12px box corner for boxes that grow in order to keep them box-shaped objects by the relation: a pill control gives way to the box corner. A moderate radius does this by curving the corners while the sides stay straight as the box grows. So a text area or a list item stays a box, not an oval, because controls are pills (shape.values) and the brand is bold (brand.q1).

radius.24: We use a 24px corner for cards, menus and dialogs in order to make each offer read as a separate object, in a bold tone by brand convention. A large radius does this by breaking the outline with a wide curve while the sides stay straight. So each offer reads as one friendly object, because containers get their own corner (shape.count) and the brand is bold (brand.q1).

taupe.light.150: We use the step between 100 and 200 of the taupe ramp in light, in order to keep one step set on every ramp in both modes. The step does this by sitting even in contrast between its neighbours, on the scheme's even-ease step curve. So light and dark offer the same steps, because the gray ramp sets the steps (color.definition).

taupe.light.0: We use light's step 0 for the floor in order to keep the neutral scale whole in light. The step does this by naming white, as nothing sits above it and no light role reads the floor. So light pages stay as they are, because the floor exists for dark wells below the canvas (theming.values) and the gray ramp sets the steps (color.definition).
neutral.50, under content: 1.05:1 from surface.default, so cards and panels stand forward.
neutral.0: the base for content; body text reads 18.0:1 on it, above the 4.5:1 floor.
neutral.0, the same as content (surface.default): a menu stands out by its edge and its one shadow, not by its fill.

neutral.0: We use white, as raised, for menus, dialogs, sheets and toasts in light, in order to keep a floating layer as plain as the content it covers. The fill does this by staying white while its shadow lifts it off the page. So visitors see what floats without a tint of its own, because the roles answer names the layers that rise (elevation.roles).
neutral.100, a step below content (1.13:1 on surface.default), so table headers and wells read as recessed.

neutral.100, two steps darker than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.0), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band without lifting off the page. It skips neutral.50, the page canvas, so a menu item never matches the page behind it.
neutral.200, one step past the highlight (neutral.100), so a press reads as its own change under the finger: pressed for touch.

shadow.card: We use step 1 of the shadow scale for cards in order to show their height as objects above the page. The cast shade does this by a 12px offset and a 32px blur at 14%. So each offer feels like an object you can pick up, because cards rise too (elevation.roles) and shadows are pronounced (elevation.values).

shadow.overlay: We use step 2 of the shadow scale for menus and dialogs in order to show floating height, one step above the cards. The cast shade does this by a 24px offset and a 48px blur at 20%, larger than the card's. So a menu sits clearly above vivid sections and cards, because cards and overlays rise (elevation.roles) and shadows are pronounced (elevation.values).

The step does this by its place on the scheme's even-ease curve, which spaces the dark steps by contrast. So a table header reads as recessed even on the page itself, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and the gray ramp sets the steps (color.definition).
neutral.0, under content: 1.08:1 from surface.default, so cards and panels stand forward.
neutral.50: the base for content; body text reads 17.12:1 on it, above the 4.5:1 floor.

neutral.100: We use one step lighter than content for parts that rise inside the page in dark, in order to show height by tone, 1.21:1 on surface.default. The lighter fill does this by the dark-mode depth rule: the higher a layer sits, the lighter its surface. Menus, dialogs and other floating layers take the next step up (surface.floating). So visitors see what rises inside the page by its tone, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and the roles answer names the layers that rise (elevation.roles).

neutral.150: We use one step lighter than raised for menus, dialogs, sheets and toasts in dark, in order to show that they float above everything else, 1.17:1 on surface.raised. The lighter fill does this by the dark-mode depth rule, and keeps what sits on it readable: body text reads 12.11:1, muted text 4.74:1, and dividers and the ring stay lighter at 1.19:1. So visitors read a menu as well as the page under it, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and the roles answer names the layers that rise (elevation.roles).

neutral.floor: We use the floor step, below the page's canvas, for table headers and wells in dark, in order to show depth by tone, 1.13:1 under content and 1.05:1 under the canvas. The darker fill does this by the depth rule turned downward: what sits lower is darker. So a well reads as recessed and never as a raised card, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and depth reads from tone and lines (elevation.definition).

neutral.floor: We use the floor step, below the canvas, for the item under the pointer or the keyboard in dark, in order to mark it as a band on the surfaces it meets: 1.13:1 on surface.default, 1.37:1 on surface.raised and 1.6:1 on surface.floating, and 1.05:1 off the page. The fill does this by stepping darker, as raised and floating layers took the lighter step; muted text still reads 7.59:1 on it. So the hovered row or menu item shows on cards and menus alike, because hover and focus have their own look (accessibility.roles) and the neutral ramp sets the steps (color.definition).

neutral.200: We use the step above the raised surface for a pressed item in dark in order to show a press as a change of its own. The fill does this by stepping lighter while the hover band steps darker, 1.91:1 from the highlight, so press and hover never match. So a tap reads under the finger, because pressed has its own look for touch (accessibility.roles) and the neutral ramp sets the steps (color.definition).

shadow.none: We use no shadow for cards in dark in order to keep shadows on floating layers only: menus, popovers, dialogs, toasts and tooltips. The missing shade does this by leaving the card's height to tone: the lighter raised surface and its 1px light ring. So cards still read as lifted on a dark page, without a shade that cannot be seen, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and cards rise by shadow in light (elevation.roles).

shadow.overlay-dark: We use the light overlay shadow's shape in dark in order to show the same floating height by the dark-shade relation. The cast shade does this by the same 24px offset and 48px blur, at 60% black instead of 20%. So a menu still sits above dark sections, though its shade reads weaker on dark than in light, because cards and overlays rise (elevation.roles) and dark ships as standard (theming.values).

neutral.why: A warm, rosy gray sits under the vivid pink brand without competing.
